subject: KMS access domains, HSM provisioning and operator separation — architecture playbook
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-security.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — key segregation, HSM provisioning & operator separation

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this on. Acme's security team is trying to lock down the final architecture for our Redwood Private deployment (on-prem in our VPC). A few top-level needs:

- Customer-managed keys (we want BYOK import or wrapped key material into an HSM).
- Strong operator separation: distinct roles for HSM operator, platform admin, and application/service accounts.
- Rotation windows with minimal downtime and cryptographic escrow / split-key option for legal escrow requirements.
- Audit trail requirements: immutable KMS logs forwarded to our SIEM and 7+ years retention.

Can you share a concise playbook of recommended access domains (who holds keys, who can request unwrap, emergency access flow), supported HSM models and provisioning flow, and the suggested rotation policy (frequency, staged rollouts, and rollback). I attached a rough requirements doc (acme_requirements_v1.pdf).

We'd like to run a canary key import and test in the week of Mar 8. Also please include any limits around key import formats (PKCS#8 vs raw key shares) and whether Redwood supports remote attestation for the HSM.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Security Architect — Acme Corp
acme-security.com

Attachment: acme_requirements_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-security.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — key segregation, HSM provisioning & operator separation

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list. High level summary and proposed next steps below; I'll attach a short CSV that lays out the access domains and who/what belongs to each. Vivek (cc'd) will own the HSM provisioning details. Mina will review compliance evidence requirements once we have the plan.

High-level approach (quick):
- Access domains: Operator (HSM provisioning & firmware), KMS Admin (policy & key lifecycle), App Service Accounts (encryption/decryption via wrapped keys), Audit/SIEM (log consumer).
- HSM options: We support customer HSMs from major vendors (Thales/Luna, nCipher); we also support cloud-HSM-backed KMS (AWS KMS custom key store) for hybrid setups. If you want on-prem tamper-resistant modules, we recommend Luna SA 8 or nCipher nShield as they support split-key import and remote attestation.
- BYOK/import: We support PKCS#8 and split-key share ingestion via an import ceremony. For legal escrow, we can provide a split-key escrow flow where Redwood holds one share and Acme retains the remaining shares (or vice versa).
- Rotation/rollback: Recommend quarterly rotation for encryption root keys; staged rollouts (canary namespace -> 20% services -> 100%) with automatic fallback to previous key on verification failure. For short-lived signing keys, recommend monthly.
- Audit & retention: Forward KMS audit events (key import, key use, admin changes) to your SIEM over TLS; recommend immutable storage/Write-Once buckets and 7 years retention.

Attachments: proposed_key_domains.csv (simple mapping of roles -> credentials -> typical actions)

Next steps from our side: Vivek will provide the provisioning playbook (HSM factory provisioning checklist, remote attestation, network segmentation for HSM mgmt), Mina will pull the compliance evidence list, and I'll propose a time for the canary import in the week of Mar 8.

Would you like us to run the import ceremony on your site or within a controlled Redwood lab that we can invite your observers into? Lab runs let us pre-seed devices without impacting your network.

Thanks — talk soon,
Rachel Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_key_domains.csv (csv)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-security.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — key segregation, HSM provisioning & operator separation

Rachel / Alex —

Adding technical detail to Rachel's summary:

1) Provisioning checklist (high level):
  - Network: HSM mgmt plane must be on a dedicated management VLAN with host-based ACLs; separate from application data plane.
  - Physical: HSMs installed in locked racks with tamper seals; console port accessible only via OOB (out-of-band) jump host.
  - Admin accounts: Two-person control for critical ops (dual-auth for key import/unseal).
  - Firmware: Factory to FIPS-validated firmware; record image signatures during provisioning.

2) Import/escrow options:
  - PKCS#8 import: supported via import ceremony into HSM; recommended when you control the full key lifecycle.
  - Split-key (Shamir-like) option: we can accept key shares and reconstruct inside the HSM under dual-control. Useful for legal escrow — we recommend 3-of-5 splits where Acme holds 2 shares and Redwood holds 1 (optional).

3) Rotation mechanics:
  - Stage rollout: create new data-encryption-key (DEK) under new root KEK -> rewrap existing DEKs and test against canary services.
  - Monitoring: 1-minute token latency and error-rate thresholds trigger automatic pause and rollback.

4) Remote attestation & tamper evidence:
  - Supported on Luna SA via hardware attestation APIs; recommend attestation before accepting imported key material.

I'll draft a provisioning playbook (step-by-step) and an operator handoff matrix (who may sign which ceremony step). Rachel, I used your confluence link as the target for drafts.

-Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team —

Couple of compliance items to call out so they can be baked into the playbook:

- Evidence list: KMS configuration exports, attestation reports, firmware image checksums, CPS (certificate practice statement) snapshots, operator access logs, and SIEM ingestion confirmation. I've attached a template checklist.
- Audit retention: Confirmed Acme needs 7-year immutable retention for key-use logs — we will recommend a WORM-backed bucket (S3 Object Lock or equivalent on-prem).
- Roles & least privilege: We should adopt role-based access maps with time-bound grants for emergency use (e.g., break-glass tickets with automated multi-party approval).
- Legal escrow: If Acme opts for split-key escrow, we need documented chain-of-custody and notarized transfer events for any share transference.

I'll populate the compliance_evidence_checklist.xlsx and add references to SOC2 controls that map to each evidence item. Once Vivek posts the provisioning playbook I'll annotate the sections that map to evidence collection points.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
